message:
fix(viewer): a given-up AU is tombstoned, so its late chunks cannot re-create it and block the head again

GiveUpIncomplete only erased the assembly. The host was still sending that AU's chunks, and the
next one walked past the stale guard and re-created it -- the head was blocked again, the same
(generation, seq) was abandoned two and three times, and the good IDR behind it never got through.
The verifying Claude found this in the passing runs too; the sweep failure was the product defect
surfacing, not a harness fault as the previous commit's history said.

The identity is now remembered instead: a bounded tombstone (16 entries, 5 s when the caller
passes a clock, cleared by Reset) blocks exactly that (generation, seq), so late data and FEC
chunks of it are ignored while everything else -- another generation, other seqs, the delivery gap
and IDR recovery contract -- is untouched. lastDeliveredSeq_ is deliberately NOT moved forward:
claiming the AU was delivered would change what the next delivery reports as a gap and could
swallow AUs nobody judged.

The regressions asserted on keyframe requests, which the request limiter squeezes to one or two
whatever happens, so the repeat was invisible. The receiver's give-up counter is exposed through
RecvStats and S17/S18/S21/S23/S24 now assert exactly one give-up per head; S24 is new (late chunks
after a give-up: ignored, no second give-up, the recovery IDR still arrives) and the shared-core
unit covers the tombstone's identity, ttl and Reset rules. S23 now paces chunks at 30 ms so the
hard cap is what ends it. history #419, with #417 corrected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
